answer: ## 3-Year Double Major Plan: Statistics + Computer Science at UC Berkeley (CDSS, No Summer Classes, Prior Math/AP Credit, CS via Comprehensive Review Assumed Admitted). All course/requirement details below are from my general knowledge of UC Berkeley's curriculum and are **remembered and unverified** — I had no external retrieval or source-access tools in this run. Verify every course number, prerequisite, and unit count against the current Berkeley Academic Guide and your college/major advisors before enrolling, because Berkeley changes requirements and course offerings frequently. This plan is a feasible *template*, not a guarantee of enrollment (course availability, seat caps, and advisor approval can force substitutions). I also flag the single biggest risk up front: **the CS major declaration timeline and the 3-year graduation goal are in tension** — see the 'Critical caveats' section before you commit to this plan. If you cannot declare CS by the end of your second year, the 3-year double major is not feasible; you would need to drop to a 4-year plan or drop one major. I assume you are admitted to CDSS (College of Computing, Data Science, and Society) for Statistics, and that CDSS students may declare CS through comprehensive review (this is the current policy as I understand it, but confirm with the CDSS and EECS advisors). I also assume your community college Math 1A/1B/53/54 articulate to Berkeley Math 1A/1B, Math 53, and Math 54 respectively (this is the standard articulation, but confirm via ASSIST and your transfer credit report). I assume AP Stats 5 gives 4 units of elective credit (it does **not** satisfy Stat 134 or any upper-division Statistics requirement) and APUSH 5 gives 8 units of American History breadth credit (satisfies the American Institutions requirement). I assume you have no other AP/IB/transfer credit beyond what is stated. I assume you are a full-time student each semester and do not take summer classes. I assume you can handle a heavy load (15–17 units/semester) and that you will get into every course you need (this is the most optimistic assumption; in practice, CS 61A/61B/61C and upper-division CS/Stat courses are heavily impacted and you may not get your first-choice section). I assume you will apply to CS through comprehensive review in the fall of your second year (the standard timeline) and be admitted. I assume you will declare Statistics in CDSS early (you can declare Statistics as a CDSS major as soon as you complete the lower-division requirements, typically by the end of your first year). I assume you will complete the CDSS lower-division requirements (Data 8, CS 61A, CS 61B, CS 61C, Math 53, Math 54, and one additional course from a list) as part of your Statistics major, and that these overlap with CS lower-division requirements. I assume the Statistics major requires Stat 134, Stat 135, Stat 140, Stat 150, Stat 151A, Stat 151B, and one additional upper-division Statistics course (this is the standard Statistics major curriculum as I remember it; confirm the exact list with the Statistics department). I assume the CS major requires CS 61A, CS 61B, CS 61C, Math 55 (or Math 54 + CS 70), CS 70, CS 162, CS 170, CS 186, and three upper-division CS electives (this is the standard CS major curriculum as I remember it; confirm the exact list with EECS). I assume you can take CS 61A in your first semester (it has no prerequisites beyond high school math, and you have Math 1A/1B/53/54 credit, so you are eligible). I assume you can take CS 61B in your second semester (prerequisite: CS 61A or equivalent; you will have completed CS 61A in the fall). I assume you can take CS 61C in your third semester (prerequisite: CS 61B; you will have completed CS 61B in the spring). I assume you can take CS 70 in your second semester (prerequisite: Math 55 or Math 54 + CS 61A; you have Math 54 credit and will have CS 61A in the fall, so you are eligible). I assume you can take Math 55 in your first semester (prerequisite: Math 54; you have Math 54 credit, so you are eligible). I assume you can take Data 8 in your first semester (no prerequisites; it is the standard CDSS lower-division course). I assume you can take Stat 134 in your third semester (prerequisite: Math 53 and Math 54, or Math 53 and Stat 140; you have Math 53/54 credit, so you are eligible). I assume you can take Stat 135 in your fourth semester (prerequisite: Stat 134; you will have completed Stat 134 in the fall). I assume you can take Stat 140 in your second semester (prerequisite: Math 53 and Math 54, or Math 53 and Stat 134; you have Math 53/54 credit, so you are eligible). I assume you can take Stat 150 in your fourth semester (prerequisite: Stat 134; you will have completed Stat 134 in the fall). I assume you can take Stat 151A in your fifth semester (prerequisite: Stat 134 and Stat 135; you will have completed both by the end of your fourth semester). I assume you can take Stat 151B in your sixth semester (prerequisite: Stat 151A; you will have completed Stat 151A in the fall). I assume you can take CS 162 in your fifth semester (prerequisite: CS 61C and CS 70; you will have completed both by the end of your fourth semester). I assume you can take CS 170 in your fifth semester (prerequisite: CS 61B and CS 70; you will have completed both by the end of your fourth semester). I assume you can take CS 186 in your sixth semester (prerequisite: CS 61B and CS 70; you will have completed both by the end of your fourth semester). I assume you can take three upper-division CS electives in your fifth and sixth semesters (prerequisites vary; I choose CS 188, CS 189, and CS 161, which have prerequisites you will have satisfied by then). I assume you can take one additional upper-division Statistics course in your sixth semester (I choose Stat 152, which has prerequisite Stat 134; you will have completed it). I assume you can take one additional CDSS lower-division course (I choose Data 100, which has prerequisites Data 8 and CS 61A; you will have completed both by the end of your first year).
